title: Boil the Hound Once It Caught the Hares
synopsis: Liu Bang becomes the first emperor of the Han Dynasty but is increasingly paranoid about those around him.

fullText.simplified:
兔死狗烹

    刘邦做了汉朝的第一位皇帝后，一时之间，真是快活极了。汉朝可是秦朝以后的第一个大国，他再也不是一个小小的汉王，而成了高高在上的“汉高祖”。
   这位新皇帝从平民中来，最明白老百姓的艰难。他从秦朝的失败中吸取教训，决定要好好照顾老百姓，少收一些税。慢慢地，原本很穷的国家有了生机，变得欣欣向荣起来。
    此时，仗打完了，刘邦表彰了那些帮助过他的人，给了自己的手下很多奖赏。
    刘邦有一个手下叫张良。自从刘邦当上皇帝以后，他突然变得奇奇怪怪的。隔不了几天，他就要请一次病假，在家里休息，不去工作。大臣们都很奇怪：“张大人身体怎么又不好了？”
    其实张良是装病，他并没有什么不舒服的地方。他请假在家，喝酒、玩耍，快活得很。当别人有事问他的时候，他就随口胡说，谁也不知道他的真实想法。
    刘邦表彰手下，想赠送一块地给他，张良却坚决不要，只要了他和刘邦认识的那个小县城。至于其他人，有些人功劳不如张良大，得到的土地却比张良多、官位比张良大；有些人功劳和张良差不多，就接受奖赏，做了大王。很多人觉得张良是不是老了，变愚蠢了，到手的好处竟然不要？
    其实，张良才是最明智的那个。他最了解刘邦，最知道刘邦的心事。
    原来，当上“汉高祖”的刘邦一直有个心结。打天下难，守好天下更难。刘邦可不想和前面几位皇帝一样，做一个短命皇帝。尤其是因为刘邦自己就曾经是项羽的手下，听命于项羽，最后却打败了项羽。现在刘邦做了皇帝，最怕的也不是别人，正是那些跟他一起打江山的手下们！在刘邦看来，这些手下不是他的兄弟、儿子，他们都是“外人”。他害怕这些外人终有一天，会像他打败项羽那样，把他给杀了。
    正如张良料想的那样，不久后，刘邦终于忍不住开始动手了。他先是下令把以前项羽的那些手下杀了，然后又把目光放在了那几个新上任的“大王”身上。因为那几个大王，不是刘邦的兄弟、儿子，地位却比刘邦的亲人还尊贵。
    刘邦第一个要杀的大王，以前跟随过项羽。在刘邦的手段之下，他不想死，就只能匆忙造反，三个月之后就被杀死了。
    一年之后，刘邦又以造反的理由，抓走了第二个大王——韩信。韩信是刘邦的大将军，帮他做过很多事。可以说，没有韩信，刘邦就不可能当上皇帝。当韩信发觉刘邦想要杀他后，他不服气地说道：“你怎么这么没有良心？猎狗帮你抓到了野兔，现在野兔死光了，你觉得猎狗没用了，就要煮猎狗吃了吗？弓箭帮你打天上的鸟儿，现在鸟儿打尽了，你觉得弓箭没用了，就要抛弃弓箭了吗？我帮你打败了项羽，让你当了皇帝，现在你觉得我没用了，就要对我这样的功臣下手了吗？”
    听了这样的话，刘邦又不好意思杀韩信了，只是收回了给韩信的奖赏，把他关起来了。但一段时间后，刘邦还是找机会杀了韩信。
    渐渐地，几个大王和很多功臣就这样被刘邦杀完了，只有张良没有被杀。他舒服地活到了六十多岁，最后病死了。
    韩信和刘邦说的那个关于野兔和猎狗的比喻，有个成语叫做“兔死狗烹”。到了今天，如果有人在成功以后，又去陷害帮助过自己的人，人们就会说这是“兔死狗烹”。譬如：老王在老李最困难的时候，借钱给老李，他们一起开了公司。等公司越来越好后，老李却赶走了老王，真是“兔死狗烹”啊！
fullText.traditional:
兔死狗烹

    劉邦做了漢朝的第一位皇帝後，一時之間，真是快活極了。漢朝可是秦朝以後的第一個大國，他再也不是一個小小的漢王，而成了高高在上的“漢高祖”。
   這位新皇帝從平民中來，最明白老百姓的艱難。他從秦朝的失敗中吸取教訓，決定要好好照顧老百姓，少收一些稅。慢慢地，原本很窮的國家有了生機，變得欣欣向榮起來。
    此時，仗打完了，劉邦表彰了那些幫助過他的人，給了自己的手下很多獎賞。
    劉邦有一個手下叫張良。自從劉邦當上皇帝以後，他突然變得奇奇怪怪的。隔不了幾天，他就要請一次病假，在家裡休息，不去工作。大臣們都很奇怪：“張大人身體怎麼又不好了？”
    其實張良是裝病，他並沒有什麼不舒服的地方。他請假在家，喝酒、玩耍，快活得很。當別人有事問他的時候，他就隨口胡說，誰也不知道他的真實想法。
    劉邦表彰手下，想贈送一塊地給他，張良卻堅決不要，只要了他和劉邦認識的那個小縣城。至於其他人，有些人功勞不如張良大，得到的土地卻比張良多、官位比張良大；有些人功勞和張良差不多，就接受獎賞，做了大王。很多人覺得張良是不是老了，變愚蠢了，到手的好處竟然不要？
    其實，張良才是最明智的那個。他最瞭解劉邦，最知道劉邦的心事。
    原來，當上“漢高祖”的劉邦一直有個心結。打天下難，守好天下更難。劉邦可不想和前面幾位皇帝一樣，做一個短命皇帝。尤其是因為劉邦自己就曾經是項羽的手下，聽命於項羽，最後卻打敗了項羽。現在劉邦做了皇帝，最怕的也不是別人，正是那些跟他一起打江山的手下們！在劉邦看來，這些手下不是他的兄弟、兒子，他們都是“外人”。他害怕這些外人終有一天，會像他打敗項羽那樣，把他給殺了。
    正如張良料想的那樣，不久後，劉邦終於忍不住開始動手了。他先是下令把以前項羽的那些手下殺了，然後又把目光放在了那幾個新上任的“大王”身上。因為那幾個大王，不是劉邦的兄弟、兒子，地位卻比劉邦的親人還尊貴。
    劉邦第一個要殺的大王，以前跟隨過項羽。在劉邦的手段之下，他不想死，就只能匆忙造反，三個月之後就被殺死了。
    一年之後，劉邦又以造反的理由，抓走了第二個大王——韓信。韓信是劉邦的大將軍，幫他做過很多事。可以說，沒有韓信，劉邦就不可能當上皇帝。當韓信發覺劉邦想要殺他後，他不服氣地說道：“你怎麼這麼沒有良心？獵狗幫你抓到了野兔，現在野兔死光了，你覺得獵狗沒用了，就要煮獵狗吃了嗎？弓箭幫你打天上的鳥兒，現在鳥兒打盡了，你覺得弓箭沒用了，就要拋棄弓箭了嗎？我幫你打敗了項羽，讓你當了皇帝，現在你覺得我沒用了，就要對我這樣的功臣下手了嗎？”
    聽了這樣的話，劉邦又不好意思殺韓信了，只是收回了給韓信的獎賞，把他關起來了。但一段時間後，劉邦還是找機會殺了韓信。
    漸漸地，幾個大王和很多功臣就這樣被劉邦殺完了，只有張良沒有被殺。他舒服地活到了六十多歲，最後病死了。
    韓信和劉邦說的那個關於野兔和獵狗的比喻，有個成語叫做“兔死狗烹”。到了今天，如果有人在成功以後，又去陷害幫助過自己的人，人們就會說這是“兔死狗烹”。譬如：老王在老李最困難的時候，借錢給老李，他們一起開了公司。等公司越來越好後，老李卻趕走了老王，真是“兔死狗烹”啊！

sentences.simplified: 正是那些跟他一起打江山的手下们！
sentences.traditional: 正是那些跟他一起打江山的手下們！
sentences.pinyin: zhèng shì nà xiē gēn tā yì qǐ dǎ jiāng shān de shǒu xià men
sentences.english: Now that Liu Bang was emperor, he was not afraid of other people.

sentences.simplified: 在刘邦看来，这些手下不是他的兄弟、儿子，他们都是“外人”。
sentences.traditional: 在劉邦看來，這些手下不是他的兄弟、兒子，他們都是“外人”。
sentences.pinyin: zài liú bāng kàn lái zhè xiē shǒu xià bú shì tā de xiōng dì ér zi tā men dōu shì wài rén
sentences.english: Rather, he was most afraid of the very men that fought under him to seize power!

sentences.simplified: 他害怕这些外人终有一天，会像他打败项羽那样，把他给杀了。
sentences.traditional: 他害怕這些外人終有一天，會像他打敗項羽那樣，把他給殺了。
sentences.pinyin: tā hài pà zhè xiē wài rén zhōng yǒu yì tiān huì xiàng tā dǎ bài xiàng yǔ nà yàng bǎ tā gěi shā le
sentences.english: In Liu Bang’s eyes, these men were not his brothers nor his sons. They were all all “outsiders”.
He was afraid that one day these outsiders would kill him, just like how he defeated Xiang Yu.

sentences.simplified: 正如张良料想的那样，不久后，刘邦终于忍不住开始动手了。
sentences.traditional: 正如張良料想的那樣，不久後，劉邦終於忍不住開始動手了。
sentences.pinyin: zhèng rú zhāng liáng liào xiǎng de nà yàng bù jiǔ hòu liú bāng zhōng yú rěn bú zhù kāi shǐ dòng shǒu le

sentences.simplified: 他先是下令把以前项羽的那些手下杀了，然后又把目光放在了那几个新上任的“大王”身上。
sentences.traditional: 他先是下令把以前項羽的那些手下殺了，然後又把目光放在了那幾個新上任的“大王”身上。
sentences.pinyin: tā xiān shì xià lìng bǎ yǐ qián xiàng yǔ de nà xiē shǒu xià shā le rán hòu yòu bǎ mù guāng fàng zài le nà jǐ ge xīn shàng rèn de dà wáng shēn shang
sentences.english: Just as Zhang Liang thought, soon after, Liu Bang couldn’t resist any longer and began to make moves.

sentences.simplified: 因为那几个大王，不是刘邦的兄弟、儿子，地位却比刘邦的亲人还尊贵。
sentences.traditional: 因為那幾個大王，不是劉邦的兄弟、兒子，地位卻比劉邦的親人還尊貴。
sentences.pinyin: yīn wèi nà jǐ ge dà wáng bú shì liú bāng de xiōng dì ér zi dì wèi què bǐ liú bāng de qīn rén hái zūn guì
sentences.english: He first ordered those who worked under Xiang Yu to be killed, and then he set his gaze on the newly appointed “kings”.
This was because those kings were not Liu Bang’s brothers or sons, and yet their status was more noble than Liu Bang’s close relatives.

sentences.simplified: 刘邦第一个要杀的大王，以前跟随过项羽。
sentences.traditional: 劉邦第一個要殺的大王，以前跟隨過項羽。
sentences.pinyin: liú bāng dì yī ge yào shā de dà wáng yǐ qián gēn suí guò xiàng yǔ

sentences.simplified: 在刘邦的手段之下，他不想死，就只能匆忙造反，三个月之后就被杀死了。
sentences.traditional: 在劉邦的手段之下，他不想死，就只能匆忙造反，三個月之後就被殺死了。
sentences.pinyin: zài liú bāng de shǒu duàn zhī xià tā bù xiǎng sǐ jiù zhǐ néng cōng máng zào fǎn sān ge yuè zhī hòu jiù bèi shā sǐ le
sentences.english: The first king that Liu Bang wanted to kill had previously been under Xiang Yu.
He did not want to die at the hands of Liu Bang. He could only hastily rebel and was killed three months later.

sentences.simplified: 一年之后，刘邦又以造反的理由，抓走了第二个大王——韩信。
sentences.traditional: 一年之後，劉邦又以造反的理由，抓走了第二個大王——韓信。
sentences.pinyin: yì nián zhī hòu liú bāng yòu yǐ zào fǎn de lǐ yóu zhuā zǒu le dì èr ge dà wáng hán xìn

sentences.simplified: 韩信是刘邦的大将军，帮他做过很多事。
sentences.traditional: 韓信是劉邦的大將軍，幫他做過很多事。
sentences.pinyin: hán xìn shì liú bāng de dà jiāng jūn bāng tā zuò guò hěn duō shì
sentences.english: One year later, Liu Bang again used rebellion as a justification and captured the second king—Han Xin.

sentences.simplified: 可以说，没有韩信，刘邦就不可能当上皇帝。
sentences.traditional: 可以說，沒有韓信，劉邦就不可能當上皇帝。
sentences.pinyin: kě yǐ shuō méi yǒu hán xìn liú bāng jiù bù kě néng dāng shàng huáng dì
sentences.english: Han Xin was Liu Bang’s important general and helped him do many things.

sentences.simplified: 当韩信发觉刘邦想要杀他后，他不服气地说道：“你怎么这么没有良心？
sentences.traditional: 當韓信發覺劉邦想要殺他後，他不服氣地說道：“你怎麼這麼沒有良心？
sentences.pinyin: dāng hán xìn fā jué liú bāng xiǎng yào shā tā hòu tā bù fú qì de shuō dào nǐ zěn me zhè me méi yǒu liáng xīn
sentences.english: It can be said that without Han Xin, there was no way Liu Bang could have become emperor.

sentences.simplified: 猎狗帮你抓到了野兔，现在野兔死光了，你觉得猎狗没用了，
sentences.traditional: 獵狗幫你抓到了野兔，現在野兔死光了，你覺得獵狗沒用了，
sentences.pinyin: liè gǒu bāng nǐ zhuā dào le yě tù xiàn zài yě tù sǐ guāng le nǐ jué de liè gǒu méi yòng le
sentences.english: When Han Xin realized that Liu Bang wanted to kill him, he said defiantly, “How could you be so heartless?

sentences.simplified: 就要煮猎狗吃了吗？
sentences.traditional: 就要煮獵狗吃了嗎？
sentences.pinyin: jiù yào zhǔ liè gǒu chī le ma
sentences.english: The hound helped you catch the hares, and now that the hares are dead, you think the hound is useless.

sentences.simplified: 弓箭帮你打天上的鸟儿，现在鸟儿打尽了，
sentences.traditional: 弓箭幫你打天上的鳥兒，現在鳥兒打盡了，
sentences.pinyin: gōng jiàn bāng nǐ dǎ tiān shàng de niǎo'r xiàn zài niǎo'r dǎ jìn le
sentences.english: So, you want to cook the hound and eat it?

sentences.simplified: 你觉得弓箭没用了，就要抛弃弓箭了吗？
sentences.traditional: 你覺得弓箭沒用了，就要拋棄弓箭了嗎？
sentences.pinyin: nǐ jué de gōng jiàn méi yòng le jiù yào pāo qì gōng jiàn le ma
sentences.english: The bow and arrow helped you shoot the birds in the sky, and now all the birds have been shot, ..

sentences.simplified: 我帮你打败了项羽，让你当了皇帝，现在你觉得我没用了，
sentences.traditional: 我幫你打敗了項羽，讓你當了皇帝，現在你覺得我沒用了，
sentences.pinyin: wǒ bāng nǐ dǎ bài le xiàng yǔ ràng nǐ dāng le huáng dì xiàn zài nǐ jué de wǒ méi yòng le
sentences.english: .. you think the bow and arrow are useless, so you want to abandon them?

sentences.simplified: 就要对我这样的功臣下手了吗？”
sentences.traditional: 就要對我這樣的功臣下手了嗎？”
sentences.pinyin: jiù yào duì wǒ zhè yàng de gōng chén xià shǒu le ma
sentences.english: I helped you defeat Xiang Yu, which allowed you to become emperor, but now you think I’m useless.
So, you want to go after an official who has given outstanding service like me?”

sentences.simplified: 听了这样的话，刘邦又不好意思杀韩信了，
sentences.traditional: 聽了這樣的話，劉邦又不好意思殺韓信了，
sentences.pinyin: tīng le zhè yàng de huà liú bāng yòu bù hǎo yì si shā hán xìn le

sentences.simplified: 只是收回了给韩信的奖赏，把他关起来了。
sentences.traditional: 只是收回了給韓信的獎賞，把他關起來了。
sentences.pinyin: zhǐ shì shōu huí le gěi hán xìn de jiǎng shǎng bǎ tā guān qǐ lái le
sentences.english: After hearing such words, Liu Bang felt too embarrassed to kill Han Xin.

sentences.simplified: 但一段时间后，刘邦还是找机会杀了韩信。
sentences.traditional: 但一段時間後，劉邦還是找機會殺了韓信。
sentences.pinyin: dàn yí duàn shí jiān hòu liú bāng hái shi zhǎo jī huì shā le hán xìn
sentences.english: Instead, he took away Han Xin’s rewards and locked him up.
But after a period of time, Liu Bang found another opportunity to kill Han Xin.

sentences.simplified: 渐渐地，几个大王和很多功臣就这样被刘邦杀完了，
sentences.traditional: 漸漸地，幾個大王和很多功臣就這樣被劉邦殺完了，
sentences.pinyin: jiàn jiàn de jǐ ge dà wáng hé hěn duō gōng chén jiù zhè yàng bèi liú bāng shā wán le

sentences.simplified: 只有张良没有被杀。
sentences.traditional: 只有張良沒有被殺。
sentences.pinyin: zhǐ yǒu zhāng liáng méi yǒu bèi shā
sentences.english: Gradually, several kings and many officials who had given outstanding service were killed by Liu Bang in this manner.

sentences.simplified: 他舒服地活到了六十多岁，最后病死了。
sentences.traditional: 他舒服地活到了六十多歲，最後病死了。
sentences.pinyin: tā shū fu de huó dào le liù shí duō suì zuì hòu bìng sǐ le
sentences.english: Only Zhang Liang was not killed.
He lived comfortably into his sixties and finally died of illness.

sentences.simplified: 韩信和刘邦说的那个关于野兔和猎狗的比喻，有个成语叫做“兔死狗烹”。
sentences.traditional: 韓信和劉邦說的那個關於野兔和獵狗的比喻，有個成語叫做“兔死狗烹”。
sentences.pinyin: hán xìn hé liú bāng shuō de nà ge guān yú yě tù hé liè gǒu de bǐ yù yǒu ge chéng yǔ jiào zuò tù sǐ gǒu pēng

sentences.simplified: 到了今天，如果有人在成功以后，又去陷害帮助过自己的人，
sentences.traditional: 到了今天，如果有人在成功以後，又去陷害幫助過自己的人，
sentences.pinyin: dào le jīn tiān rú guǒ yǒu rén zài chéng gōng yǐ hòu yòu qù xiàn hài bāng zhù guò zì jǐ de rén
sentences.english: There is an idiom for the analogy of the hares and the hound that Han Xin told Liu Bang: “boiling the hound once it caught the hares”.

sentences.simplified: 人们就会说这是“兔死狗烹”。
sentences.traditional: 人們就會說這是“兔死狗烹”。
sentences.pinyin: rén men jiù huì shuō zhè shì tù sǐ gǒu pēng
sentences.english: Today, if after achieving success, a person betrays those that helped him the past, ..

sentences.simplified: 譬如：老王在老李最困难的时候，借钱给老李，他们一起开了公司。
sentences.traditional: 譬如：老王在老李最困難的時候，借錢給老李，他們一起開了公司。
sentences.pinyin: pì rú lǎo wáng zài lǎo lǐ zuì kùn nan de shí hou jiè qián gěi lǎo lǐ tā men yì qǐ kāi le gōng sī
sentences.english: .. people will say this is “boiling the hound once it caught the hares”.

sentences.simplified: 等公司越来越好后，老李却赶走了老王，
sentences.traditional: 等公司越來越好後，老李卻趕走了老王，
sentences.pinyin: děng gōng sī yuè lái yuè hǎo hòu lǎo lǐ què gǎn zǒu le lǎo wáng
sentences.english: For example, when Old Li was going through a very difficult time, Old Wang lent him money, and they started a business together.

sentences.simplified: 真是“兔死狗烹”啊！
sentences.traditional: 真是“兔死狗烹”啊！
sentences.pinyin: zhēn shi tù sǐ gǒu pēng a
sentences.english: After the company started doing better and better, Old Li kicked Old Wang out.

sentence_translations: Boil the Hound Once It Caught the Hares
After Liu Bang became the first emperor of the Han Dynasty, he was extremely happy for a while.
The Han Dynasty was the first great power after the Qin Dynasty.
He was no longer the minor King of Han but the lofty “Emperor Gaozu of Han”.
This new emperor came from a family of commoners, so he knew very well the hardships of ordinary people.
Learning from the failures of the Qin Dynasty, he decided that he would take good care of the common people and collect fewer taxes.
Slowly, the previously poor country came to life and began to thrive.
The war was now over. Liu Bang honored those who had helped him in the past, giving many rewards to those who worked under him.
Liu Bang had a man working under him named Zhang Liang.
After Liu Bang became emperor, Zhang Liang suddenly began acting strangely.
Every few days, he would take sick leave and rest at home rather than work.
The ministers all found this strange: “Why is Lord Zhang in poor health again?”
In reality, Zhang Liang was feigning illness. He wasn’t in any discomfort.
He took time off to stay at home, drink, and play around. He was having a great time.
When people came to him with problems, he would just come out with nonsense. No one knew his true thoughts.
Liu Bang, who was honoring those working under him, wanted to give Zhang Liang a piece of land.
Zhang Liang adamantly refused. He only wanted the small county town where he and Liu Bang met.
As for the other people, some people’s contributions were not as big as Zhang Liang’s.
However, they received more land than him and got higher positions than him.
Some people’s contributions were similar to Zhang Liang’s. They accepted their rewards and became kings.
Many people thought that Zhang Liang was getting old and becoming stupid.
Why would he refuse benefits that were handed to him?
But actually, Zhang Liang was the wisest one. He knew Liu Bang the best, and he knew best what Liu Bang was thinking.
It turns out that Liu Bang, who became “Emperor Gaozu of Han”, had always had a nagging thought.
It is difficult to fight the world, but it is even more difficult to retain the world.
Liu Bang did not want to be like the previous few emperors and have a short-lived reign.
This was especially because Liu Bang himself had once worked under Xiang Yu.
He took orders from Xiang Yu yet eventually defeated him.
Now that Liu Bang was emperor, he was not afraid of other people.
Rather, he was most afraid of the very men that fought under him to seize power!
In Liu Bang’s eyes, these men were not his brothers nor his sons. They were all all “outsiders”.
He was afraid that one day these outsiders would kill him, just like how he defeated Xiang Yu.
Just as Zhang Liang thought, soon after, Liu Bang couldn’t resist any longer and began to make moves.
He first ordered those who worked under Xiang Yu to be killed, and then he set his gaze on the newly appointed “kings”.
This was because those kings were not Liu Bang’s brothers or sons, and yet their status was more noble than Liu Bang’s close relatives.
The first king that Liu Bang wanted to kill had previously been under Xiang Yu.
He did not want to die at the hands of Liu Bang. He could only hastily rebel and was killed three months later.
One year later, Liu Bang again used rebellion as a justification and captured the second king—Han Xin.
Han Xin was Liu Bang’s important general and helped him do many things.
It can be said that without Han Xin, there was no way Liu Bang could have become emperor.
When Han Xin realized that Liu Bang wanted to kill him, he said defiantly, “How could you be so heartless?
The hound helped you catch the hares, and now that the hares are dead, you think the hound is useless.
So, you want to cook the hound and eat it?
The bow and arrow helped you shoot the birds in the sky, and now all the birds have been shot, ..
.. you think the bow and arrow are useless, so you want to abandon them?
I helped you defeat Xiang Yu, which allowed you to become emperor, but now you think I’m useless.
So, you want to go after an official who has given outstanding service like me?”
After hearing such words, Liu Bang felt too embarrassed to kill Han Xin.
Instead, he took away Han Xin’s rewards and locked him up.
But after a period of time, Liu Bang found another opportunity to kill Han Xin.
Gradually, several kings and many officials who had given outstanding service were killed by Liu Bang in this manner.
Only Zhang Liang was not killed.
He lived comfortably into his sixties and finally died of illness.
There is an idiom for the analogy of the hares and the hound that Han Xin told Liu Bang: “boiling the hound once it caught the hares”.
Today, if after achieving success, a person betrays those that helped him the past, ..
.. people will say this is “boiling the hound once it caught the hares”.
For example, when Old Li was going through a very difficult time, Old Wang lent him money, and they started a business together.
After the company started doing better and better, Old Li kicked Old Wang out.
This is truly “boiling the hound once it caught the hares“!
